### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class), migrateStoredMetadata (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f47f7f222f1c8c03ab866efa428f4b50ff72b9b8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0c1ecfc677c8a454a36d35d6c860207d544bcbde` — the merge of head `aa0ca3a339eb4c6fada43313722da119f1244f6c` into base `f47f7f222f1c8c03ab866efa428f4b50ff72b9b8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0c1ecfc677c8a454a36d35d6c860207d544bcbde && git checkout 0c1ecfc677c8a454a36d35d6c860207d544bcbde
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f47f7f222f1c8c03ab866efa428f4b50ff72b9b8 aa0ca3a339eb4c6fada43313722da119f1244f6c && git checkout -B drift-repro f47f7f222f1c8c03ab866efa428f4b50ff72b9b8 && git merge --no-ff aa0ca3a339eb4c6fada43313722da119f1244f6c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f47f7f222f1c8c03ab866efa428f4b50ff72b9b8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f47f7f222f1c8c03ab866efa428f4b50ff72b9b8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `aa0ca3a339eb4c6fada43313722da119f1244f6c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/conversions/apply.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts + packages/spec/src/data/external-binding-datasource.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/index.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.external-binding-named-datasource-refusal.test.ts, .changeset/25279-stored-external-binding-known-datasources.md

Inputs read: card #25279 (body and all three comments: claim 6350967049, claim amendment 6351011546, os-dev-report 6351912835), PR #25299 (body, 7-file list, net diff against `main` at the head), the head's check-runs, and the cited code as committed blobs at the head. Check-runs read at 2026-10-22T21:51Z: 25 success, 7 skipped (the full-battery lanes, filtered off a PR run), 8 in progress — `Test Core` 1/6 through 6/6, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates` — reported pending, not waited for. Concluded green among the gate-carrying set: `Build Core`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. The remainder of the diff outside `Scope:` (the protocol pass, the two tests, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; it is read here only where the scoped hunks make a claim about it.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **`ApplyConversionsOptions.knownDatasources` (new optional member, `ReadonlyMap` of name to `{ schemaMode?: unknown }`) — RIGHT.** `ApplyConversionsOptions` is exported from `conversions/index.ts` and recorded on the root entry (`packages/spec/api-surface/root.json`: "ApplyConversionsOptions (interface)"), so this is a widening of a published public face. `StoredConversionOptions` (the Omit of `ApplyConversionsOptions` without `includeRetired`) inherits it unchanged, so `applyConversionsToStoredItem` gains it too; `collectConversionNotices`' options type (the Omit without `onNotice`) inherits it as well (harmless: it is read only under `onTodo`). No api-surface artifact moves — the snapshot records that an export exists, never its members — and `git diff 49185cdb8..aa0ca3a33 -- packages/spec/api-surface packages/spec/api-surface-signatures.json` is empty; the claim amendment's expectation of regenerated api-surface files resolved to none needed, which is consistent, not a gap. `check:exported-any` is unaffected (`unknown`, not `any`).
2. **`applyConversions` reads the option only inside `if (onTodo)` — RIGHT.** It is destructured and handed to `reportRefusedStoredShapes(current, { knownDatasources }, …)` and nowhere else, so the authoring funnel (`normalizeStackInput`, no sink) and every read seam never touch it; the spec test pins zero `Map.get` calls without a sink.
3. **`RefusedStoredShape.detect` gains a required third `context` parameter and `reportRefusedStoredShapes` a `context` positional — RIGHT, and internal.** `refused-shapes.ts` is not re-exported from `conversions/index.ts` (its header says so and the barrel confirms it), and the only non-test caller of `reportRefusedStoredShapes` is `apply.ts:203`; no `.detect(` call exists outside the runner. The three other detectors declare two parameters and are assignable.
4. **The `external` detector still judges through the save door's own predicate over the door's own datasource set — RIGHT.** `externalBindingOnManagedDatasource.detect` resolves `definitionOf(name) = declared.get(name) ?? context.knownDatasources?.get(name)` and hands the result to `externalBindingDatasourceRefusal` (`packages/spec/src/data/external-binding-datasource.ts:90`) unchanged — no reimplementation of the judgement. For a stored object row the wrapper is `{ objects: [row] }`, so `declared` is empty and the verdict comes from the map alone. The map's one entry is produced by `storedRowKnownDatasources` → `externalBindingDatasourceDefinition(name)`, and the object half of `externalBindingSaveRefusal` (`protocol.ts:22584`) now calls that same private read, which is the pre-#25279 inline `readMetaItem({ type: 'datasource', name })?.item` moved into a function. The two therefore cannot resolve different datasources for one name: the environment's active stored row, else the code layer's definition (MetadataService registration, then registry), with `declinesStoredRow` letting a host-declared code datasource win over a residue row — the #25257 door's set exactly. Edge spellings agree too: an omitted or empty `datasource` reaches the predicate as the primary half at both sites (`''` → `undefined` map at the pass; the predicate folds `''` to `'default'`). "Listed exactly when that door refuses it" holds.
5. **The `surface` string now says what it covers — RIGHT.** "object.external — a federated binding on the primary datasource, or on a managed one the stack declares or the caller resolves (a stored or registered datasource)". It carries no tracker number (the runtime-string rule). The D3 entry's own `surface` and `acceptanceCriteria` (`18.object-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused.ts`) already said the save doors see stored and registered datasources and that `os migrate meta --stored` lists each such row; that sentence is now true, so the entry is correctly left unchanged and the card's second branch (a guidance edit naming a gap) is correctly not taken.
6. **`migrateStoredMetadata` and the datasource rows — RIGHT, by a different route than pre-gathering.** The pass does not collect datasource rows up front; for each non-flow row it awaits `storedRowKnownDatasources(singular, body)` (object rows carrying `external` and a string `datasource` only; every other row gets `undefined` at once) and reads the named datasource live through the door's read. Order of `rows[]` is therefore irrelevant, and an `--apply` run judges an object row against the datasource as it stands at that moment — which is what its next save will meet. Scope: organization-scoped object rows are reported `skipped` and `continue` before this step, and `readMetaItem` reads only the environment layer (ADR-0131 D6: no organization's row is read) — the door's scope. Retired/invalid rows: `readMetaItem` with no `state` reads `active` only, so an archived datasource row is never read and a draft datasource row is not consulted (a draft object row is judged against the active datasource, as the door judges a draft save); a non-object datasource body yields `undefined` and no verdict, as at the door. Row type is folded through `canonicalMetaType` first, so a legacy plural `objects` row is still an `object` row here.
7. **No other `applyConversions` / `applyConversionsToStoredItem` / `applyConversionsToFlow` caller changes behaviour — RIGHT.** Census at the head, non-test: `metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts:884` and `core/src/fallbacks/authored-translation-sync.ts:172` (`applyConversionsToStoredItem`, `onNotice` only, no sink); `spec/src/shared/metadata-collection.zod.ts:240` and `metadata-core/src/artifact-forward-conversion.ts:570` (`applyConversions`, no sink); `protocol.ts:7013` and `:23998` (`applyConversionsToFlow`, no sink); `service-automation` `canonicalizeStoredFlow` (`engine.ts:4570`) goes through `applyConversionsToFlow` over `{ flows: […] }`, which the `external` detector never walks. With the option absent the context is `{ knownDatasources: undefined }` and `definitionOf` falls back to `declared.get(name)` alone — byte-for-byte the prior verdict.
8. **The tests pin the card's acceptance — RIGHT.** Spec side (+7): a known datasource declared `'managed'` or with no `schemaMode` is listed once, not rewritten, with the door's own first sentence; `'external'` and `'validate-only'` are not; a name the row does not use gives no verdict; a stack-declared datasource is read before the caller's; no read without a sink. Protocol side (+6): an object row planted straight into the `sys_metadata` double (stored before the door existed) is listed `skipped` at `objects[0].external` on a stored managed datasource in both shapes, and the same body offered to `saveMetaItem` is refused `422 INVALID_METADATA` at `external` in the same environment; listed on a registered managed datasource; not listed when a stored federated row overlays a registered managed definition, and that save goes through; not listed on a federated or absent datasource (the card's control, both halves).

Observations, none blocking: (a) a datasource read that throws inside the loop aborts the pass rather than recording the row `failed` — the pass's own up-front reads and `readLegacyOrganizationRows` take the same posture, and the dev states it in the JSDoc; (b) the "registered" half is as wide as the datasource set the invoking host registers (a CLI boot versus the server), which is inherent in reusing the door's read and is not a defect; (c) `readMetaItem` on a pre-protocol datasource row logs its own conversion `warn` once per read — the door does the same.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` — TRUE.** The diff adds an optional member to a published interface on the `@objectstack/spec` root entry; that is a widening of the public face, and the arm is the closed-pair spelling. The claim expected `no`; the dev measured `yes (widening)` from the diff, which is the correct reading, and the deviation is declared in the os-dev-report and the PR body.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` — TRUE.** Nothing a metadata author can write changes: no key, accepted value, metadata type, default or meaning moves; the listing gains only rows the #25257 door already refuses, the `surface` string is operator-facing TODO prose, and no `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` shard moves.
- **`patch` for `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` — RIGHT; `minor` is NOT owed.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: "The level follows the kind alone: a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` mechanizes the same ruling (maintainer ruling A, 2026-10-21, on #25105): "`none` → every introduced entry `patch`", "A non-protocol widening (REST) or narrowing … ships `patch`", and "`none` beside a `minor` … is refused whatever the package". The earlier "a purely additive widening of a published public surface takes at least `minor`" coupling is the superseded rule that file's own header describes as re-ruled. So a new public optional member under `Metadata-protocol: none` is `patch`; a `minor` here would have been refused. `Check Changeset` on this head concluded success — the gate verdict agrees. Both declaration lines are present, line-initial, in the PR body and the changeset body; the changeset is one file, both packages in the fixed group, no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition marker, which is right for a non-narrowing `none`. `skip-changeset` would have been wrong (both packages publish, `private` unset at 18.0.0).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag: `Clause-②` deviates from the claim's expected `no`** — answered above: the measured `yes (widening)` is right; the claim itself allowed for it ("`yes (widening)` if a new public option lands; the dev measures it from the diff").
- **Dev flag: `packages/spec/src/conversions/apply.ts` added to the file surface** — right; the option cannot reach `refused-shapes.ts` except through `applyConversions`, and the claim amendment 6351011546 recorded the widening before the edit (the claim's own stop-and-explain condition met).
- **Dev flag: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally (every-package `dist` prerequisite)** — it rides the CI lint/typecheck lanes; `Lint · repo & tooling gates` has concluded success on this head, and the two `Type Check` lanes still running are reported pending above.
- **`open_questions`: empty** — nothing to answer or escalate.
- **`out_of_scope_findings` (one entry, os-dev-report 6351912835): the pass lists the external/managed pair only at the object row; the stored datasource row, whose next save the datasource door would refuse while objects bind it `external`, carries no TODO of its own. Answer: NO CARD — the PR's Acceptance notes are the right carrier.** A managed datasource is a valid row on its own; the refusal is a fact about the pair, and ADR-0087 D3 lists a pair once, under the entry that owns it (`object-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused`, path `objects[0].external`). The object row's TODO already names both fixes (declare the datasource `schemaMode: 'external'` / `'validate-only'`, or drop `external`), and either clears the datasource door too. If an `--apply` run re-saves a datasource row the chain moved, the datasource door's `422` lands as `failed` with the finding quoted — the pass's documented class "rows that still fail the current schema after conversion", loud, not silent, so there is no reproducible defect, contract violation or authoring trap to carry (Prime Directive #10's test for a card). A datasource-row TODO would need its own D3 entry and would list the same pair twice. Reach: none measured, as the dev recorded. Not escalated to the maintainer.
- **Governed surfaces**: none in the file list; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success. PR is draft with auto-merge unarmed; landing stays the lane seat's act once every required check is green.

Reviewed-by: `session_01B2EeooonSXrANpkpgUSfFZ`

**VERDICT: PASS**

The fix hands the stored pass a `knownDatasources` context read through the #25257 door's own datasource read (`externalBindingDatasourceDefinition`), so the listing and the door judge one set through one predicate.

The dev's local `dispatch-gates` run: 88 derived, 87 run with exit 0, 1 NOT-MEASURED (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, needs every package dist; left to CI), 0 UNRUN. `spec check:generated`: 14 of 14 fresh.
